data.english: Meanwhile Cyllenian Hermes called forth the spirits of the wooers.

data.english: Meanwhile Cyllenian Hermes called forth the spirits of the wooers.

data.greek: ὧν ἐθέλει, τοὺς δʼ αὖτε καὶ ὑπνώοντας ἐγείρει·
data.english: Meanwhile Cyllenian Hermes called forth the spirits of the wooers.

data.greek: τῇ ῥʼ ἄγε κινήσας, ταὶ δὲ τρίζουσαι ἕποντο.

data.greek: ὡς δʼ ὅτε νυκτερίδες μυχῷ ἄντρου θεσπεσίοιο
data.english: He held in his hands his wand, a fair wand of gold, wherewith he lulls to sleep the eyes of whom he will, while others again he wakens even out of slumber; with this he roused and led the spirits, and they followed gibbering.

data.english: He held in his hands his wand, a fair wand of gold, wherewith he lulls to sleep the eyes of whom he will, while others again he wakens even out of slumber; with this he roused and led the spirits, and they followed gibbering.

data.greek: ὁρμαθοῦ ἐκ πέτρης, ἀνά τʼ ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται,
data.english: And as in the innermost recess of a wondrous cave bats flit about gibbering, when one has fallen from off the rock from the chain in which they cling to one another, so these went with him gibbering, and Hermes, the Helper, led them down the dank ways.

data.greek: ὣς αἱ τετριγυῖαι ἅμʼ ἤϊσαν· ἦρχε δʼ ἄρα σφιν
data.english: And as in the innermost recess of a wondrous cave bats flit about gibbering, when one has fallen from off the rock from the chain in which they cling to one another, so these went with him gibbering, and Hermes, the Helper, led them down the dank ways.

data.greek: Ἑρμείας ἀκάκητα κατʼ εὐρώεντα κέλευθα.
data.english: And as in the innermost recess of a wondrous cave bats flit about gibbering, when one has fallen from off the rock from the chain in which they cling to one another, so these went with him gibbering, and Hermes, the Helper, led them down the dank ways.

data.greek: πὰρ δʼ ἴσαν Ὠκεανοῦ τε ῥοὰς καὶ Λευκάδα πέτρην,
data.english: And as in the innermost recess of a wondrous cave bats flit about gibbering, when one has fallen from off the rock from the chain in which they cling to one another, so these went with him gibbering, and Hermes, the Helper, led them down the dank ways.

data.greek: ἠδὲ παρʼ Ἠελίοιο πύλας καὶ δῆμον ὀνείρων
data.english: Past the streams of Oceanus they went, past the rock Leucas , past the gates of the sun and the land of dreams, and quickly came to the mead of asphodel, where the spirits dwell, phantoms of men who have done with toils.

data.greek: ἤϊσαν· αἶψα δʼ ἵκοντο κατʼ ἀσφοδελὸν λειμῶνα,
data.english: Past the streams of Oceanus they went, past the rock Leucas , past the gates of the sun and the land of dreams, and quickly came to the mead of asphodel, where the spirits dwell, phantoms of men who have done with toils.

data.greek: ἔνθα τε ναίουσι ψυχαί, εἴδωλα καμόντων.
data.english: Past the streams of Oceanus they went, past the rock Leucas , past the gates of the sun and the land of dreams, and quickly came to the mead of asphodel, where the spirits dwell, phantoms of men who have done with toils.

data.greek: εὗρον δὲ ψυχὴν Πηληϊάδεω Ἀχιλῆος
data.english: Here they found the spirit of Achilles, son of Peleus, and those of Patroclus, of peerless Antilochus, and of Aias, who in comeliness and form was the goodliest of all the Danaans after the peerless son of Peleus.

data.greek: καὶ Πατροκλῆος καὶ ἀμύμονος Ἀντιλόχοιο
data.english: Here they found the spirit of Achilles, son of Peleus, and those of Patroclus, of peerless Antilochus, and of Aias, who in comeliness and form was the goodliest of all the Danaans after the peerless son of Peleus.

data.greek: Αἴαντός θʼ, ὃς ἄριστος ἔην εἶδός τε δέμας τε
data.english: Here they found the spirit of Achilles, son of Peleus, and those of Patroclus, of peerless Antilochus, and of Aias, who in comeliness and form was the goodliest of all the Danaans after the peerless son of Peleus.

data.greek: τῶν ἄλλων Δαναῶν μετʼ ἀμύμονα Πηλεΐωνα.
data.english: Here they found the spirit of Achilles, son of Peleus, and those of Patroclus, of peerless Antilochus, and of Aias, who in comeliness and form was the goodliest of all the Danaans after the peerless son of Peleus.

data.greek: ὣς οἱ μὲν περὶ κεῖνον ὁμίλεον· ἀγχίμολον δὲ
data.english: So these were thronging about Achilles, and near to them drew the spirit of Agamemnon, son of Atreus, sorrowing; and round about him others were gathered, the spirits of all those who were slain with him in the house of Aegisthus, and met their fate.

data.greek: ἤλυθʼ ἔπι ψυχὴ Ἀγαμέμνονος Ἀτρεΐδαο
data.english: So these were thronging about Achilles, and near to them drew the spirit of Agamemnon, son of Atreus, sorrowing; and round about him others were gathered, the spirits of all those who were slain with him in the house of Aegisthus, and met their fate.

data.greek: ἀχνυμένη· περὶ δʼ ἄλλαι ἀγηγέραθʼ, ὅσσαι ἅμʼ αὐτῷ
data.english: So these were thronging about Achilles, and near to them drew the spirit of Agamemnon, son of Atreus, sorrowing; and round about him others were gathered, the spirits of all those who were slain with him in the house of Aegisthus, and met their fate.

data.greek: οἴκῳ ἐν Αἰγίσθοιο θάνον καὶ πότμον ἐπέσπον.
data.english: And the spirit of the son of Peleus was first to address him, saying: “Son of Atreus, we deemed that thou above all other heroes wast all thy days dear to Zeus, who hurls the thunderbolt, because thou wast lord over many mighty men in the land of the Trojans, where we Achaeans suffered woes.

data.greek: τὸν προτέρη ψυχὴ προσεφώνεε Πηλεΐωνος·
data.english: And the spirit of the son of Peleus was first to address him, saying: “Son of Atreus, we deemed that thou above all other heroes wast all thy days dear to Zeus, who hurls the thunderbolt, because thou wast lord over many mighty men in the land of the Trojans, where we Achaeans suffered woes.

data.greek: Ἀτρεΐδη, περὶ μέν σʼ ἔφαμεν Διὶ τερπικεραύνῳ
data.english: And the spirit of the son of Peleus was first to address him, saying: “Son of Atreus, we deemed that thou above all other heroes wast all thy days dear to Zeus, who hurls the thunderbolt, because thou wast lord over many mighty men in the land of the Trojans, where we Achaeans suffered woes.

data.greek: ἀνδρῶν ἡρώων φίλον ἔμμεναι ἤματα πάντα,
data.english: But verily on thee too was deadly doom to come all too early, the doom that not one avoids of those who are born.

data.greek: οὕνεκα πολλοῖσίν τε καὶ ἰφθίμοισιν ἄνασσες
data.english: But verily on thee too was deadly doom to come all too early, the doom that not one avoids of those who are born.

data.greek: δήμῳ ἔνι Τρώων, ὅθι πάσχομεν ἄλγεʼ Ἀχαιοί.
data.english: But verily on thee too was deadly doom to come all too early, the doom that not one avoids of those who are born.

data.greek: ἦ τʼ ἄρα καὶ σοὶ πρῶϊ παραστήσεσθαι ἔμελλεν
data.english: But verily on thee too was deadly doom to come all too early, the doom that not one avoids of those who are born.

data.greek: μοῖρʼ ὀλοή, τὴν οὔ τις ἀλεύεται ὅς κε γένηται.
data.english: Ah, would that in the pride of that honor of which thou wast master thou hadst met death and fate in the land of the Trojans.

data.greek: ὡς ὄφελες τιμῆς ἀπονήμενος, ἧς περ ἄνασσες,
data.english: Ah, would that in the pride of that honor of which thou wast master thou hadst met death and fate in the land of the Trojans.

data.greek: δήμῳ ἔνι Τρώων θάνατον καὶ πότμον ἐπισπεῖν·
data.english: Ah, would that in the pride of that honor of which thou wast master thou hadst met death and fate in the land of the Trojans.

data.greek: τῷ κέν τοι τύμβον μὲν ἐποίησαν Παναχαιοί,
data.english: Then would the whole host of the Achaeans have made thee a tomb, and for thy son too wouldst thou have won great glory in days to come; but now, as it seems, it has been decreed that thou shouldst be cut off by a most piteous death.” Then the spirit of the son of Atreus answered him: “Fortunate son of Peleus, godlike Achilles, that wast slain in the land of Troy far from Argos , and about thee others fell, the best of the sons of the Trojans and Achaeans, fighting for thy body; and thou in the whirl of dust didst lie mighty in thy mightiness, forgetful of thy horsemanship.

data.greek: ἠδέ κε καὶ σῷ παιδὶ μέγα κλέος ἤραʼ ὀπίσσω·
data.english: Then would the whole host of the Achaeans have made thee a tomb, and for thy son too wouldst thou have won great glory in days to come; but now, as it seems, it has been decreed that thou shouldst be cut off by a most piteous death.” Then the spirit of the son of Atreus answered him: “Fortunate son of Peleus, godlike Achilles, that wast slain in the land of Troy far from Argos , and about thee others fell, the best of the sons of the Trojans and Achaeans, fighting for thy body; and thou in the whirl of dust didst lie mighty in thy mightiness, forgetful of thy horsemanship.

data.greek: νῦν δʼ ἄρα σʼ οἰκτίστῳ θανάτῳ εἵμαρτο ἁλῶναι.
data.english: Then would the whole host of the Achaeans have made thee a tomb, and for thy son too wouldst thou have won great glory in days to come; but now, as it seems, it has been decreed that thou shouldst be cut off by a most piteous death.” Then the spirit of the son of Atreus answered him: “Fortunate son of Peleus, godlike Achilles, that wast slain in the land of Troy far from Argos , and about thee others fell, the best of the sons of the Trojans and Achaeans, fighting for thy body; and thou in the whirl of dust didst lie mighty in thy mightiness, forgetful of thy horsemanship.

data.greek: τὸν δʼ αὖτε ψυχὴ προσεφώνεεν Ἀτρείδαο·
data.english: Then would the whole host of the Achaeans have made thee a tomb, and for thy son too wouldst thou have won great glory in days to come; but now, as it seems, it has been decreed that thou shouldst be cut off by a most piteous death.” Then the spirit of the son of Atreus answered him: “Fortunate son of Peleus, godlike Achilles, that wast slain in the land of Troy far from Argos , and about thee others fell, the best of the sons of the Trojans and Achaeans, fighting for thy body; and thou in the whirl of dust didst lie mighty in thy mightiness, forgetful of thy horsemanship.

data.greek: ὄλβιε Πηλέος υἱέ, θεοῖς ἐπιείκελʼ Ἀχιλλεῦ,
data.english: We on our part strove the whole day long, nor should we ever have stayed from the fight, had not Zeus stayed us with a storm.

data.greek: ὃς θάνες ἐν Τροίῃ ἑκὰς Ἄργεος· ἀμφὶ δέ σʼ ἄλλοι
data.english: We on our part strove the whole day long, nor should we ever have stayed from the fight, had not Zeus stayed us with a storm.

data.greek: κτείνοντο Τρώων καὶ Ἀχαιῶν υἷες ἄριστοι,
data.english: We on our part strove the whole day long, nor should we ever have stayed from the fight, had not Zeus stayed us with a storm.

data.greek: μαρνάμενοι περὶ σεῖο· σὺ δʼ ἐν στροφάλιγγι κονίης
data.english: But after we had borne thee to the ships from out the fight, we laid thee on a bier, and cleansed thy fair flesh with warm water and with ointment, and many hot tears did the Danaans shed around thee, and they shore their hair.

data.greek: κεῖσο μέγας μεγαλωστί, λελασμένος ἱπποσυνάων.
data.english: But after we had borne thee to the ships from out the fight, we laid thee on a bier, and cleansed thy fair flesh with warm water and with ointment, and many hot tears did the Danaans shed around thee, and they shore their hair.

data.greek: ἡμεῖς δὲ πρόπαν ἦμαρ ἐμαρνάμεθʼ· οὐδέ κε πάμπαν
data.english: But after we had borne thee to the ships from out the fight, we laid thee on a bier, and cleansed thy fair flesh with warm water and with ointment, and many hot tears did the Danaans shed around thee, and they shore their hair.

data.greek: παυσάμεθα πτολέμου, εἰ μὴ Ζεὺς λαίλαπι παῦσεν.
data.english: But after we had borne thee to the ships from out the fight, we laid thee on a bier, and cleansed thy fair flesh with warm water and with ointment, and many hot tears did the Danaans shed around thee, and they shore their hair.

data.greek: αὐτὰρ ἐπεί σʼ ἐπὶ νῆας ἐνείκαμεν ἐκ πολέμοιο,
data.english: And thy mother came forth from the sea with the immortal sea-nymphs, when she heard the tidings, and a wondrous cry arose over the deep, and thereat trembling laid hold of all the Achaeans.

data.greek: κάτθεμεν ἐν λεχέεσσι, καθήραντες χρόα καλὸν
data.english: And thy mother came forth from the sea with the immortal sea-nymphs, when she heard the tidings, and a wondrous cry arose over the deep, and thereat trembling laid hold of all the Achaeans.

data.greek: ὕδατί τε λιαρῷ καὶ ἀλείφατι· πολλὰ δέ σʼ ἀμφὶ
data.english: And thy mother came forth from the sea with the immortal sea-nymphs, when she heard the tidings, and a wondrous cry arose over the deep, and thereat trembling laid hold of all the Achaeans.

data.greek: δάκρυα θερμὰ χέον Δαναοὶ κείροντό τε χαίτας.
data.english: Then would they all have sprung up and rushed to the hollow ships, had not a man, wise in the wisdom of old, stayed them, even Nestor, whose counsel had before appeared the best.

data.greek: μήτηρ δʼ ἐξ ἁλὸς ἦλθε σὺν ἀθανάτῃς ἁλίῃσιν
data.english: Then would they all have sprung up and rushed to the hollow ships, had not a man, wise in the wisdom of old, stayed them, even Nestor, whose counsel had before appeared the best.

data.greek: ἀγγελίης ἀΐουσα· βοὴ δʼ ἐπὶ πόντον ὀρώρει
data.english: Then would they all have sprung up and rushed to the hollow ships, had not a man, wise in the wisdom of old, stayed them, even Nestor, whose counsel had before appeared the best.

data.greek: θεσπεσίη, ὑπὸ δὲ τρόμος ἔλλαβε πάντας Ἀχαιούς·
data.english: He with good intent addressed their assembly, and said: “‘Hold, ye Argives; flee not, Achaean youths.

data.greek: καί νύ κʼ ἀναΐξαντες ἔβαν κοίλας ἐπὶ νῆας,
data.english: He with good intent addressed their assembly, and said: “‘Hold, ye Argives; flee not, Achaean youths.

data.greek: εἰ μὴ ἀνὴρ κατέρυκε παλαιά τε πολλά τε εἰδώς,
data.english: He with good intent addressed their assembly, and said: “‘Hold, ye Argives; flee not, Achaean youths.

data.greek: Νέστωρ, οὗ καὶ πρόσθεν ἀρίστη φαίνετο βουλή·
data.english: He with good intent addressed their assembly, and said: “‘Hold, ye Argives; flee not, Achaean youths.

data.greek: ὅ σφιν ἐϋφρονέων ἀγορήσατο καὶ μετέειπεν·
data.english: 'Tis his mother who comes here forth from the sea with the immortal sea-nymphs to look upon the face of her dead son.’ “So he spoke, and the great-hearted Achaeans ceased from their flight.

data.greek: ἴσχεσθʼ, Ἀργεῖοι, μὴ φεύγετε, κοῦροι Ἀχαιῶν·
data.english: 'Tis his mother who comes here forth from the sea with the immortal sea-nymphs to look upon the face of her dead son.’ “So he spoke, and the great-hearted Achaeans ceased from their flight.

data.greek: μήτηρ ἐξ ἁλὸς ἥδε σὺν ἀθανάτῃς ἁλίῃσιν
data.english: 'Tis his mother who comes here forth from the sea with the immortal sea-nymphs to look upon the face of her dead son.’ “So he spoke, and the great-hearted Achaeans ceased from their flight.

data.greek: ἔρχεται, οὗ παιδὸς τεθνηότος ἀντιόωσα.
data.english: Then around thee stood the daughters of the old man of the sea wailing piteously, and they clothed thee about with immortal raiment.

data.greek: ὣς ἔφαθʼ, οἱ δʼ ἔσχοντο φόβου μεγάθυμοι Ἀχαιοί·
data.english: Then around thee stood the daughters of the old man of the sea wailing piteously, and they clothed thee about with immortal raiment.

data.greek: ἀμφὶ δέ σʼ ἔστησαν κοῦραι ἁλίοιο γέροντος
data.english: Then around thee stood the daughters of the old man of the sea wailing piteously, and they clothed thee about with immortal raiment.

data.greek: οἴκτρʼ ὀλοφυρόμεναι, περὶ δʼ ἄμβροτα εἵματα ἕσσαν.
data.english: Then around thee stood the daughters of the old man of the sea wailing piteously, and they clothed thee about with immortal raiment.

data.greek: Μοῦσαι δʼ ἐννέα πᾶσαι ἀμειβόμεναι ὀπὶ καλῇ
data.english: And the Muses, nine in all, replying to one another with sweet voices, led the dirge.

data.greek: θρήνεον· ἔνθα κεν οὔ τινʼ ἀδάκρυτόν γʼ ἐνόησας
data.english: And the Muses, nine in all, replying to one another with sweet voices, led the dirge.

data.greek: Ἀργείων· τοῖον γὰρ ὑπώρορε Μοῦσα λίγεια.
data.english: And the Muses, nine in all, replying to one another with sweet voices, led the dirge.

data.greek: ἑπτὰ δὲ καὶ δέκα μέν σε ὁμῶς νύκτας τε καὶ ἦμαρ
data.english: There couldst thou not have seen an Argive but was in tears, so deeply did the clear-toned Muse move their hearts.

data.greek: κλαίομεν ἀθάνατοί τε θεοὶ θνητοί τʼ ἄνθρωποι·
data.english: There couldst thou not have seen an Argive but was in tears, so deeply did the clear-toned Muse move their hearts.

data.greek: ὀκτωκαιδεκάτῃ δʼ ἔδομεν πυρί, πολλὰ δέ σʼ ἀμφὶ
data.english: There couldst thou not have seen an Argive but was in tears, so deeply did the clear-toned Muse move their hearts.

data.greek: μῆλα κατεκτάνομεν μάλα πίονα καὶ ἕλικας βοῦς.
data.english: There couldst thou not have seen an Argive but was in tears, so deeply did the clear-toned Muse move their hearts.

data.greek: καίεο δʼ ἔν τʼ ἐσθῆτι θεῶν καὶ ἀλείφατι πολλῷ
data.english: Thus for seventeen days alike by night and day did we bewail thee, immortal gods and mortal men, and on the eighteenth we gave thee to the fire, and many well-fatted sheep we slew around thee and sleek kine.

data.greek: καὶ μέλιτι γλυκερῷ· πολλοὶ δʼ ἥρωες Ἀχαιοὶ
data.english: Thus for seventeen days alike by night and day did we bewail thee, immortal gods and mortal men, and on the eighteenth we gave thee to the fire, and many well-fatted sheep we slew around thee and sleek kine.

data.greek: τεύχεσιν ἐρρώσαντο πυρὴν πέρι καιομένοιο,
data.english: Thus for seventeen days alike by night and day did we bewail thee, immortal gods and mortal men, and on the eighteenth we gave thee to the fire, and many well-fatted sheep we slew around thee and sleek kine.

data.greek: πεζοί θʼ ἱππῆές τε· πολὺς δʼ ὀρυμαγδὸς ὀρώρει
data.english: So thou wast burned in the raiment of the gods and in abundance of unguents and sweet honey; and many Achaean warriors moved in their armour about the pyre, when thou wast burning, both footmen and charioteers, and a great din arose.

data.greek: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ δή σε φλὸξ ἤνυσεν Ἡφαίστοιο,
data.english: So thou wast burned in the raiment of the gods and in abundance of unguents and sweet honey; and many Achaean warriors moved in their armour about the pyre, when thou wast burning, both footmen and charioteers, and a great din arose.

data.greek: ἠῶθεν δή τοι λέγομεν λεύκʼ ὀστέʼ, Ἀχιλλεῦ,
data.english: So thou wast burned in the raiment of the gods and in abundance of unguents and sweet honey; and many Achaean warriors moved in their armour about the pyre, when thou wast burning, both footmen and charioteers, and a great din arose.

data.greek: οἴνῳ ἐν ἀκρήτῳ καὶ ἀλείφατι· δῶκε δὲ μήτηρ
data.english: But when the flame of Hephaestus had made an end of thee, in the morning we gathered thy white bones, Achilles, and laid them in unmixed wine and unguents.

data.greek: χρύσεον ἀμφιφορῆα· Διωνύσοιο δὲ δῶρον
data.english: But when the flame of Hephaestus had made an end of thee, in the morning we gathered thy white bones, Achilles, and laid them in unmixed wine and unguents.

data.greek: φάσκʼ ἔμεναι, ἔργον δὲ περικλυτοῦ Ἡφαίστοιο.
data.english: But when the flame of Hephaestus had made an end of thee, in the morning we gathered thy white bones, Achilles, and laid them in unmixed wine and unguents.

data.greek: ἐν τῷ τοι κεῖται λεύκʼ ὀστέα, φαίδιμʼ Ἀχιλλεῦ,
data.english: But when the flame of Hephaestus had made an end of thee, in the morning we gathered thy white bones, Achilles, and laid them in unmixed wine and unguents.

data.greek: μίγδα δὲ Πατρόκλοιο Μενοιτιάδαο θανόντος,
data.english: Thy mother had given a two-handled, golden urn, and said that it was the gift of Dionysus, and the handiwork of famed Hephaestus.

data.greek: χωρὶς δʼ Ἀντιλόχοιο, τὸν ἔξοχα τῖες ἁπάντων
data.english: Thy mother had given a two-handled, golden urn, and said that it was the gift of Dionysus, and the handiwork of famed Hephaestus.

data.greek: τῶν ἄλλων ἑτάρων, μετὰ Πάτροκλόν γε θανόντα.
data.english: Thy mother had given a two-handled, golden urn, and said that it was the gift of Dionysus, and the handiwork of famed Hephaestus.

data.greek: ἀμφʼ αὐτοῖσι δʼ ἔπειτα μέγαν καὶ ἀμύμονα τύμβον
data.english: In this lie thy white bones, glorious Achilles, and mingled with them the bones of the dead Patroclus, son of Menoetius, but apart lie those of Antilochus, whom thou didst honor above all the rest of thy comrades after the dead Patroclus.

data.greek: χεύαμεν Ἀργείων ἱερὸς στρατὸς αἰχμητάων
data.english: In this lie thy white bones, glorious Achilles, and mingled with them the bones of the dead Patroclus, son of Menoetius, but apart lie those of Antilochus, whom thou didst honor above all the rest of thy comrades after the dead Patroclus.

data.greek: ἀκτῇ ἔπι προὐχούσῃ, ἐπὶ πλατεῖ Ἑλλησπόντῳ,
data.english: In this lie thy white bones, glorious Achilles, and mingled with them the bones of the dead Patroclus, son of Menoetius, but apart lie those of Antilochus, whom thou didst honor above all the rest of thy comrades after the dead Patroclus.

data.greek: ὥς κεν τηλεφανὴς ἐκ ποντόφιν ἀνδράσιν εἴη
data.english: In this lie thy white bones, glorious Achilles, and mingled with them the bones of the dead Patroclus, son of Menoetius, but apart lie those of Antilochus, whom thou didst honor above all the rest of thy comrades after the dead Patroclus.

data.greek: τοῖς οἳ νῦν γεγάασι καὶ οἳ μετόπισθεν ἔσονται.

data.greek: οὔ τι καταισχύνοντα τεὸν γένος, ὡς ἀγορεύεις.
data.english: But when they had clothed their bodies in gleaming bronze, they opened the doors and went forth, and Odysseus led them.

data.greek: ὣς φάτο, Λαέρτης δʼ ἐχάρη καὶ μῦθον ἔειπε·

data.greek: υἱός θʼ υἱωνός τʼ ἀρετῆς πέρι δῆριν ἔχουσιν.
data.english: Then Athena, daughter of Zeus, drew near them in the likeness of Mentor both in form and in voice, and the much-enduring, goodly Odysseus was glad at sight of her, and straightway spoke to Telemachus, his dear son: “Telemachus, now shalt thou learn this—having thyself come to the place of battle, where the best warriors are put to the trial—to bring no disgrace upon the house of thy fathers, for we have ever excelled in strength and in valor over all the earth.” And wise Telemachus answered him: “Thou shalt see me, if thou wilt, dear father, in my present temper, bringing no disgrace upon thy house, even as thou sayest.” So said he, and Laertes was glad, and spoke, saying: “What a day is this for me, kind gods!

data.greek: αἶψα μαλʼ ἀμπεπαλὼν προΐει δολιχόσκιον ἔγχος.
data.english: Verily right glad am I: my son and my son's son are vying with one another in valor.” Then flashing-eyed Athena came near him and said: “Son of Arceisius, far the dearest of all my friends, make a prayer to the flashing-eyed maiden and to father Zeus, and then straightway raise aloft thy long spear, and hurl it.” So spoke Pallas Athena, and breathed into him great might.

data.english: Then he prayed to the daughter of great Zeus, and straightway raised aloft his long spear, and hurled it, and smote Eupeithes through the helmet with cheek-piece of bronze.

data.english: Then on the foremost fighters fell Odysseus and his glorious son, and thrust at them with swords and double-pointed spears.

data.greek: ὥς κεν ἀναιμωτί γε διακρινθῆτε τάχιστα.
data.english: And now would they have slain them all, and cut them off from returning, had not Athena, daughter of Zeus, who bears the aegis, shouted aloud, and checked all the host, saying: “Refrain, men of Ithaca , from grievous war, that with all speed you may part, and that without bloodshed.” So spoke Athena, and pale fear seized them.

data.greek: καὶ τότε δὴ Κρονίδης ἀφίει ψολόεντα κεραυνόν,
data.english: Terribly then shouted the much-enduring, goodly Odysseus, and gathering himself together he swooped upon them like an eagle of lofty flight, and at that moment the son of Cronos cast a flaming thunderbolt, and down it fell before the flashing-eyed daughter of the mighty sire.
